newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE plans to rejig share conditions.
newsitem.headline: RWE plans to rejig share conditions.

text.p: Diversified German utility group RWE AG said on Wednesday it planned to alter the conditions of its shares, subject to shareholder approval.
RWE said in a statement it aimed to convert its registered common stock, with additional voting rights, into bearer common shares carrying standard voting rights.

Because voting rights would become available as a result of this move, RWE said holders of preferred shares would be given the option of swapping their shares for common shares with standard voting rights.
The total number of votes would not change as a result of these measures, RWE said.
RWE said the conversion of preferred shares would take place on a voluntary basis at a cost which had not yet been calculated.
The payments would be transferred to holders of registered shares to compensate them for the loss of additional voting rights.
The cost of conversion would be calculated on the basis of the average long term price differential between RWE's preferred and common stock.
RWE said it was inviting its shareholders in the public sector, the holders of most of its registered shares, to start talks on its proposal.
